preamble: Spirantization of the voiceless aspirated velar stop [kʰ] to the velar fricative [x], usually together with the other members of an aspirated series. Greek χ, an aspirate [kʰ] in Classical Attic, had become a fricative by about the 4th century AD, and Proto-Indo-Iranian *kʰ became Proto-Iranian *x (Sanskrit sákhā vs. Avestan haxa 'friend').

examples.to: [x] (Modern Greek χώρα [ˈxora]); [ç] before front vowels, χείρ /kʰěːr/ > /ˈçir/
examples.note: Rome catacomb inscriptions of the 2nd–3rd centuries still point to /kʰ/; Codex Vaticanus (4th century) gives strong evidence for fricative χ.
The Proto-Indo-Iranian voiceless aspirates *pʰ, *tʰ, *kʰ were spirantized to *f, *θ, *x in most Iranian languages.
